internal.title: SEV1 Incident: High Error Rate in Checkout Service Due to Payment Service Fault
internal.body:
At 11:55 UTC on 2026-11-08, an alert was triggered for a high error rate in the checkout service. Diagnosis identified a high error rate (50%) in the payment service caused by an error injection fault as the root cause. The frontend and checkout services also showed elevated error rates, indicating cascading impact.

Actions taken included disabling the paymentFailure flag at 12:15 UTC after approval, which led to rapid recovery and normalization of error rates across all affected services.

Timeline:
- 11:55:33 UTC: Alert received for checkout service error rate spike.
- 12:15:16 UTC: Diagnosis confirmed payment service error injection.
- 12:15:21 UTC: PaymentFailure flag disabled after approval.
- 12:15:21 UTC: Recovery verified with error rates returning to normal.

This incident highlights the importance of monitoring interdependent services and rapid flag management to mitigate cascading failures.

external.title: Some checkouts failed due to payment service issues
external.body:
Between 11:55 and 12:15 UTC on 2026-11-08, some customers experienced issues completing checkout due to a problem in the payment processing service. The issue was identified and resolved promptly, and normal service was restored shortly after.

We apologize for any inconvenience caused and appreciate your understanding.

output.impact: Customers experienced failures completing checkout during the incident window, impacting transaction success rates.
output.root_cause: An error injection fault in the payment service caused a high error rate, which cascaded to the checkout and frontend services.
output.resolution: The paymentFailure feature flag was disabled after approval, which stopped the error injection and restored normal service operation.

lessons.lesson: Monitor dependent services closely for error propagation and have rapid flag management processes in place to mitigate cascading failures.
lessons.applies_when: When a dependent service shows a high error rate causing cascading failures in checkout.
